chapter_mission: Breathing room chapter. Day four in hyperspace, six people in a ship for two. Kael laughs for the first time anyone has heard. Ben and Desh finally name what they did in GAG and what Jacen became. Approach to Maetha's Training Facility; Sera recognises Gavran's personal seal notation on the scan.
chapter_turn: Two pieces of silent history become speech. Kael's laugh announces that he is present, not just aboard; Ben and Desh's GAG conversation surfaces the pattern-recognition that will later let Ben see through Torin. The chapter's pace slows so the book's emotional infrastructure can set.

scene_plan.purpose: Day four. The ship smells like six people in a space for two. Desh keeps an ironic tally of arguments on his datapad. Sera and Torin disagree about galley rotation. Kael laughs at something Desh says — short, genuine, cut off — and the whole ship notices. Later, Desh drops into the co-pilot seat next to Ben with studied casualness and waits until the cockpit door closes.

Cockpit, night cycle. Desh does not start with Jacen. He starts with a specific day — a raid they both remember, an arrest that went wrong, a face Ben sees when he cannot sleep. The GAG history acknowledged. Then Desh: 'He sounds like Jacen. The good version. Before.' Ben's stomach drops because Desh just said what Ben has been refusing to think. Neither says 'we should watch Torin.' They do not need to. PP02 pays; the Jacen-parallel structural throughline is now active between them.

Approach to Maetha's Training Facility. Desh adjusts the vector; sensor readings spike with a pattern no previous node has shown. The Force ahead is not thinned — it is flexible, boundary shimmering. Sera pulls her hands back from the console when she sees Gavran's personal seal notation. 'This was Maetha's.' The name means nothing to Ben. Her expression says it should. H11 plants.

relationship_turns.to: named co-survivors — the GAG history between them is now in the open, and with it the framework that will let Ben see Torin clearly in Ch18. This is the book's second most important private conversation
first visible belonging — Kael's laugh is a threshold crossing, observed by everyone, commented on by none
warmth becoming mechanical — Ben now has the vocabulary to register that Torin's stories arrive on too-perfect timing. He does not act on it yet

exit_vector: Maetha's compound materialising in the viewport — geometric, austere, high-altitude. The Force ahead is flexible rather than thinned. Sera at the sensor panel, her hand off the controls. Gavran's seal notation glowing where no modern symbol would register. The caravan's next stop is the one the man who built the seal sealed separately.
notes: Jacen parallel touchpoint 2 (emotional). The Ben/Desh conversation is one of the book's load-bearing scenes; it is the only way the Ch18 pattern-recognition has earned ground to stand on. Keep it quiet — dim cockpit, controls they are not watching, long pauses. Avoid melodrama. The specificity of Desh's opening (a particular raid, a particular arrest, a particular face) is more affecting than any general grief. Kael's laugh in s1 is a single line and a cut — do not describe him smiling at length. Torin's warmth-becoming-mechanical is the subtlest note in the chapter; it must be felt before named — a story that hits its beats slightly too cleanly, a compliment landed slightly too perfectly. Voice: Allston-warm throughout s1, Stover-interior-permitted for the Ben/Desh scene (single paragraph max), Zahn-procedural in s3. Anti-patterns: (a) do not spell out the GAG raid — fragments only; (b) no one on-page names 'the Jacen pattern' yet except as 'he sounds like Jacen'; (c) Sera's recognition of Maetha in s3 is a charged silence, not a backstory dump.
